learning.learning_goal: Hear number words, see numerals, and count objects to ten without skipping or repeating.
learning.big_idea: The final number said when counting tells how many objects are there.

screens.label: Start here
screens.title: How many dots?
screens.body: First, hear and see the numbers. Then count dots to find how many there are.

visual.ariaLabel: Three blue dots labeled 1, 2, 3. Tap each dot to hear its number.
visual.message: Tap each dot, starting on the left. You will hear its number.

screens.title: How many dots are here?

visual.ariaLabel: Three blue dots in a row.
visual.message: Look at each dot as you count: one, two, three.

choices.feedback: Look at the dot on the right, too.
There are three dots. You said three when you reached the last dot.
Check that you did not count a dot twice.

hints: Start with the dot on the left. Move to the next dot as you count.
Which number did you say at the last dot?

visual.ariaLabel: Three blue dots together inside a box. This is one group of three dots.
visual.message: These dots are together in one box. We call them a group. There are three dots in this group.

visual.ariaLabel: Four blue dots labeled 1 through 4. Tap each dot to hear its number.
visual.message: Tap the dots from left to right. The last dot says four. There are four dots.

screens.title: How many dots are in this group?

visual.ariaLabel: Four blue dots together in one box.
visual.message: Count the dots. What number do you say at the last dot?

choices.feedback: Look at every dot, including the one on the right.
There are four dots in this group.
Count each dot once. Check that none was counted twice.

hints: Start at the left. Look at the next dot as you say the next number.
The number at the last dot tells how many dots are in the group.

visual.ariaLabel: Five blue dots labeled 1 through 5. Tap each dot in order to hear its number.
visual.message: Tap the dots from left to right to hear their numbers.

screens.title: Count to find how many.
screens.body: Look at each dot once. The number you say at the last dot tells how many dots are in the group.

screens.title: How many dots are in this group?

visual.message: Count the dots in this box. Choose how many there are.

choices.feedback: Look at the dot on the right. Count it too.
Check that each dot was counted only once.
There are five dots in this group.

hints: Look from left to right. Count every dot once.
Which number did you say when you reached the last dot?

visual.ariaLabel: Ten dots labeled in order from 1 to 10.
visual.message: Tap each dot in order to hear its number. Stop at ten.

screens.title: How many dots?

visual.ariaLabel: Dot, dot, dot, dot, dot, dot, dot, dot, dot, dot.
visual.message: Count every dot once. Which number do you say at the last dot?

choices.feedback: You may have missed a dot. Start at the left.
There are ten dots. Ten is the number at the last dot.
You may have counted a dot twice.

hints: Look at the next dot as you count from left to right.
Count every dot just once, including the last dot.

screens.title: What does the last number tell you?
screens.prompt: You counted four dots: one, two, three, four. What does four tell you?

choices.feedback: Yes. Four is how many dots you counted.

hints: Think about all the dots together.
You counted the dots. What were you trying to find?

screens.title: Count a different group.

visual.ariaLabel: Six blue dots together inside one box.
visual.message: How many dots are in this group?

choices.feedback: Check that you counted each dot only once.
Look for a dot you may have missed.
There are six dots. Six is the number at the last dot.

hints: Start at the left. Count every dot once.
Which number did you say when you reached the last dot?

screens.title: What is a group?
screens.prompt: In this lesson, the dots inside one box are together. What do we call them?
hints: Think of the dots together inside the box.
We call dots together a group.

screens.title: You counted the dots.
screens.body: Next, learn what a pair is by putting two dots together.
